items.title: Inflation has averaged 4% over the past 65 months. Under Powell, to make up for past inflation being too low, the Fed adopted a policy of targeting an average inflation rate of 2%. Consistent with that policy we now need 0% inflation for 65 months to bring the average down to 2%.

items.title: Retail sales unexpectedly fell 0.6% in July, the biggest monthly drop since May 2025. The drop in real spending is greater, as retail sales aren't inflation adjusted. When consumers pay more but buy less, living standards fall. A rising cost of living raises nominal retail sales.

items.title: The slightly better than expected PPI report means nothing regarding future inflation, which is headed much higher. As with CPI, the improvement came from comparing the average monthly price of energy products, which went down, rather than the month-end prices, which went way up.
